title: State minimum wages and cost of living
gist: As of 2026 the federal minimum wage remains $7.25 while DC and 30 states set higher rates (median $11.85), but adjusting for regional price parities materially erodes real purchasing power — DC's $18.40 falls to $16.74 and New Hampshire's $7.25 to $6.96.

insights.claim: The US federal minimum wage has held at $7.25 per hour, while Washington DC and 30 of the 50 states set higher minimums, giving a state median (including DC) of $11.85 in 2026.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Wide state dispersion above a stagnant federal floor means labor-cost exposure for low-wage employers (retail, food service) is a state-by-state map, not a single national number.
insights.quote: Washington DC and 30 of the 50 US states have minimum wages higher than the federal minimum. The median minimum wage for US states, including DC, is currently $11.85.

insights.claim: In 2026 the highest US state minimum wage is $18.40 in DC and the lowest above-federal rate is $8.75 in West Virginia, with gray-shaded states at or below the $7.25 federal rate.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: A ~$11 spread between the top and bottom state minimums flags where minimum-wage-dependent business models face the steepest cost pressure.
insights.quote: As of 2026, the highest of these state minimum wages is $18.40 in DC and the lowest is $8.75 in West Virginia.
insights.locator: Other colors indicate the state minimum wage

insights.claim: Regional price parities benchmark each state's price level against a national average of 100: California is highest at 110.72 (prices ~10.7% above average) and Arkansas lowest at 86.94 (~13.1% below).
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: RPPs let investors normalize nominal wage, cost, and consumer-spending data across states to real terms — a ~24-point CA-vs-AR gap changes how a headline wage or price translates locally.
insights.quote: California is highest, at 110.72, which means prices there are 10.7% higher than the national average. Arkansas is lowest, at 86.94, with prices about 13.1% lower than average.

insights.claim: State-level RPPs mask meaningful intra-state variation: Florida's statewide RPP is 103.41, ranging from 95.47 in the Tampa area to 103.56 in Miami.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Metro-level price dispersion within a single state warns against using state averages as a proxy for local purchasing power in site or wage analysis.
insights.quote: Florida’s RPP is 103.41. Within the state, though, RPPs vary from 95.47 in the Tampa area to 103.56 in the Miami area.
insights.locator: Note that state-level RPPs are an average

insights.claim: Adjusting nominal minimums by RPP reveals real purchasing power gaps: DC's leading $18.40 drops about $1.66 to $16.74, while New Hampshire's $7.25 falls to $6.96 after adjustment.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Real (RPP-adjusted) minimum wages compress the nominal spread — high-cost states give back part of their higher wage, a lens for judging real consumer spending power by location.
insights.quote: DC has the highest minimum wage, but also a high cost of living. Its minimum wage value drops by about $1.66 to $16.74 once adjusted by its RPP.
insights.locator: Adjusting the minimum wage by RPPs
